Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt

Interface HostFunction

All Superinterfaces:
Callable
All Known Implementing Classes:
HostFunction.Adaptor
public interface HostFunction extends Callable
A Java or Kotlin function published into a Mandela global table.

This is the whole of the host boundary. A script sees a Callable exactly like the one its own fun declarations produce, so println and fib are called the same way; the machine only needs one extra branch to tell a host function from a closure.

Implementations are usually a method reference or a Kotlin lambda, which is what makes the language "compatible with Java / Kotlin" in practice rather than in name only:


 // Java
 HostFunction.of("upper", 1, args -> String.valueOf(args.get(0)).toUpperCase())

 // Kotlin
 HostFunction.of("upper", 1) { (it[0] as String).uppercase() }

A host function may throw. Anything other than a MandelaError is wrapped as a HostError by the machine, so script code can still catch it with try / catch and the interpreter never unwinds past a catch the author wrote.
